full_judgment:
15. In order to ascertain the burden of proof in this case we may refer section 101 of the Evidence Act wherein the burden of proof has been explained. 

 "101: Burden of proof: Whoever desires any Court to give judgment as of facts which he asserts must prove that those facts exist. 

 When a person is bound to prove the existence of any fact, it is said that the burden of proof lies on that person. The burden of proof lies on the party who substantially asserts the affirmative of the issue and not upon the party who denies it. 

 16. The party on whom the onus of proof lies must, in order to succeed, establish a prima facie case. He cannot, on failure to do so take advantage of the weakness of his adversary's case. He must succeed by the strength of his own right and the clearness of his own proof. 

 27. The contesting appellant government has neither examined any witness nor has submitted any scrap of paper to substantiate his contention. The contesting appellant only filed the written statement and such statement without any oral or documentary evidence has not been proved. The contesting defendant has not even filed any paper regarding declaration of suit land as abandoned property. The contesting defendant pleaded in vague terms that the disputed property was owned as possessing by defendant No. 1 and his brother and that the defendant No. 1 and his brother being residents of Calcutta, their properties in Khulna town were declared as abandoned property and vested in the government but no document and oral evidence was adduced in support of his contention, in view of the facts and circumstances of the case, the defence has very shockingly failed to prove the case of acquisition of property as abandoned property and other burden reposed on him. 

 28. From the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record available from the plaintiffs side as has been divulged in our above discussion and observations, we without the least hesitation to hold the view that all the ingredients of benami transaction have been proved by the plaintiff as the real purchaser of the suit land under the sale deeds Exhibits 3 and 3(a) from the defendant Nos. 3 and 4; that the defendant No. 1 Ahmed Reza is his mere benamder and that the plaintiff has been in possession of the suit land in his own right as purchaser under the defendant Nos. 3 and 4. Thus, from what has been stated above we are of the view that the plaintiff has got good right, title and interest in the suit land and the burden on the plaintiff has been successfully proved. On the other hand, the contention of the contesting defendant has been hopelessly disproved.
